dialect.detail: Likely compiled with GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) on a PC/DOS or Windows environment; uses SCREEN SECTION with BACKGROUND/FOREGROUND colors, WINDOW-CREATE/WINDOW-REMOVE CONTROL strings, LINKAGE SECTION for NUMERO-CAJA and NOMBRE-USUARIO, and DOS-style backslash paths in COPY statements (e.g. DATOS\COMPROBA.FCN). Spanish-language identifiers and UI text suggest Latin American business software.
evidence: SCREEN SECTION with BACKGROUND IS BLUE FOREGROUND IS WHITE

purpose.domain_detail: Accounts receivable / customer payment collection module for a small business ERP system, likely Argentine or Latin American. Handles receipts (recibos), payment forms (formas de pago), cheques, cash register (caja), and customer ledger.
purpose.summary: This program (PAGO-CLIENTES) manages customer payment collection. It allows a cashier to enter customer invoices/vouchers to be paid, records payment details including cash, cheques, and other payment forms, and prints a receipt. It interacts with multiple indexed files for customers, vouchers, payments, cheques, bank accounts, and cash register movements.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with color attributes and WINDOW-CREATE/WINDOW-REMOVE controls
73 COPY statements referencing external copybooks (file control, file status, screen, error handlers)
LINKAGE SECTION used for inter-program parameter passing (NUMERO-CAJA, NOMBRE-USUARIO)
DECLARATIVES section with per-file error handlers via COPY
DOS/Windows backslash paths in COPY statements
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS; uses native COBOL indexed file I/O
PROCEDURE DIVISION USING clause indicating subprogram/called module
Large number of PERFORM statements (82) indicating structured modular design
Fixed-format source with occasional lines slightly over 72 chars
verdict.notes: Source truncated to first 16000 chars; DATA DIVISION not detected by mechanical scan (likely because it is entirely composed of COPY statements). Dialect is assessed as GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL based on SCREEN SECTION syntax and CONTROL string style, but could also be Micro Focus or ACU given the Windows-style paths; GnuCOBOL is most likely given the open-source context.
